[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP_Package_Individual_Application_Template.md#server-redundancy]

##### Server Redundancy

This section documents the server redundancy for [Application Service Platform]. Server redundancy refers to the amount and intensity of backup and failover or redundant servers in [Application Service Platform]. This section defines the ability of the infrastructure to provide additional servers that may be deployed on runtime for backup, load balancing, or temporarily halting of a primary server for maintenance purposes.

[Description of Application Service Platform server redundancy and backups.]
page_texts.20:
[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP_Package_Individual_Application_Template.md#ms-azure-commercial-services]

###### MS Azure Commercial Services

Weekly backups are taken of each VM allowing for system restoration of the full VM to any MS Azure Commercial Services region. Instant restore snapshots are also taken for faster recovery. The snapshots are retained for five days while the weekly backups are retained for five weeks. The snapshots are utilized for restores between the weekly backup intervals. For Structured Query Language (SQL) VMs, there is a weekly full backup taken with daily differentials for restores. SQL transaction log backups are taken every 15 minutes in order to restore SQL back to a point in time of 15-minute intervals. The VM and SQL restoration can be performed within the instance of the VM in the MS Azure Portal. From the backup menu, you can manually backup/restore the VM to the point from the desired backup or snapshot.

###### MS Azure Commercial Services

No load balancing is used for the integration servers as this is not needed for the data load processing. The MS SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS) / KingswaySoft servers pull the data that is being moved to the SFTP servers and transport it into the [Application Service Platform] instance, so there is no incoming user traffic to load balance.

page_texts.25:
[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP_Package_Individual_Application_Template.md#test-and-development-environments]

###### Test and Development Environments

In Test and Development environments, a VM is used for the SSIS and integration servers, but no clustering is setup or needed as they can be quickly restored from a backup or snapshot. The same is true with the Development environment VMs and SFTP.
page_texts.26:
[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP_Package_Individual_Application_Template.md#production-environment]

###### Production Environment

For the SSIS / KingswaySoft integration for Prod, MS SQL Server SSIS does not operate in a true failover cluster scenario by default. In newer versions of SSIS, you can use the combination of SQL Scale-out services, SQL AlwaysOn availability support, and Windows clustering in order to setup an automatic failover scenario for SQL SSIS services. In Prod, this procedure is used to setup the redundancy for the SSIS services. In this scenario, both SSIS nodes are utilizing shared storage in which both nodes can read and write to the same Database (DB); however only one node is active at a time. At the point of a primary node failure, all services are moved to the secondary SSIS node in which it becomes primary in order to keep services running.

##### Workload Locations/Facilities

[Application] uses two platforms hosted through MS. [Application] uses a MS Azure Commercial Services, Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) cloud tenant and a [Application Service Platform] tenant. The development and integration environment are hosted on VMs within an isolated client tenant within MS Azure Commercial Cloud Services. All VMs and storage related services are FedRAMP compliant. This Azure tenant is responsible for data loads and migration to the [Application Service Platform Medi-Cal tenant. The instance of [Application]for Medi-Cal is hosted with [Application Service Platform]. [Application Service Platform] is a serverless model in which the servers and network infrastructure is managed via MS but segregated from other customer cloud tenants unless network peering is in place. The user base traffic utilizes the CRM Online D365 solution internally through the Healthcare Network Cloud (HNC) network. There is an ExpressRoute Direct connection to connect the MS Azure Commercial Services tenant where the Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) and Integration servers reside.

The ExpressRoute Direct circuit connection is from the Gainwell Data Center in Tulsa to the MS Edge router in the Equinix Dallas facility and the Gainwell Data Center in Colorado Springs to the MS Edge router in the San Jose Equinix facility. Traffic from those Gainwell Data Centers use the encrypted ExpressRoute Direct port/circuit directly into the MS cloud network include [Application Service Platform].

**Disclaimer:** Due to the sensitive nature of Data Centers, the actual addresses are only made available through formal communication requests with Gainwell. Each request will be evaluated on a need-to-know basis.

#### Scheduling

This section documents the application for controlling scheduled jobs and the details of the actual scheduled jobs. A job scheduler is an application used for controlling unattended batch jobs, also known as “Batch Scheduling.” There are two types of scheduled jobs: one job occurs within [Application Service Platform] (Batch Delete) and the other is an Enterprise scheduled job to generate reports (Autosys).

1. Scheduled Jobs

| Component Name | Description | Specifications |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Batch Delete | A job that performs a purge batch delete. An internal [Application Service Platform] [Application] job that executes a query and deletes the results of that query. | A job scheduled to recur nightly at 10:00 p.m. PST. |
| Reports | A job to generate batch reports utilizing Autosys. The Autosys job executes in three steps:   1. Schedule the report 2. Execute the report 3. Distribute the report   Reference *SDP*\_[Application]*\_Appendix\_P\_Runbooks.docx* for specific details of the distribution name. | A job scheduled to recur on a monthly basis. Reports are distributed to relevant parties per the defined schedule. |

This section documents all application monitoring tools and all application sensors used for [Application].

Monitoring is achieved with MS Azure monitor and alerts that have been integrated with ServiceNow. This is a part of the Gold MS Azure Managed Service offering where the subscriptions are setup per the offering standards and service management (maintenance windows, contacts, and related information) and are documented. MS Azure Gold Services are used to align with [Application Service Platform] and MS Azure environment to the required security and compliance standards. It is used to integrate [Application] management for workflows, automation, governance, and managing VMs and storage. For more information on MS Azure Gold Services: <https://www.dxc.technology/cloud/offerings/144720/144723-managed_services_for_microsoft_azure_stack>. This is managed by the Gainwell CloudOps team.

* CMDB
* HP Network Automation (HPNA)

[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP_Package_Individual_Application_Template.md#identity-and-authentication-considerations]

### Identity and Authentication Considerations

This section documents the Identity and Authentication Considerations for D365 CSC. An effective Identity and Access Management (IAM) capability requires balancing the organization’s risk management requirements against not overcomplicating the end-user experience.

The MS Azure Commercial Services Servers access is only granted to the development team and is managed as contributor IAM access to the VMs within MS Azure Commercial Services and local admin right to the server to perform their actions. The servers within this compartment are joined to the Gainwell Medi-Cal domain hosted in ODC by the Enterprise team where no end-user access is granted or migrated to the individual servers or service portal.

D365 CSC end users are granted access to the application based on their application-based roles granted to their account for the permissions they require to perform their designated functions within the application. The D365 CSC applications authenticate using MS Azure AD as described in SDP\_CRM\_Appendix T\_Security and Auditing.docx, Section 2 Azure Active Directory.

[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP_Package_Individual_Application_Template.md#protection-considerations]

### Protection Considerations

This section documents the Protection Considerations for CRM.

D365 Customer Engagement and its portals utilize SSL encryption in transit for web and API access into its application sites. The certificates that are used are setup with the SHA-2 algorithm and use public and private keys to decrypt the in-transit requests. The browser also checks for the validity of the certificate against a certificate authority. The destination uses a symmetric key to decrypt the traffic in transit.

* <https://brightlineit.com/data-encryption-transit-business-needs-know/>
* <https://www.digicert.com/ssl/>
* <https://www.quora.com/How-is-encryption-used-to-protect-data-in-transit>
* <https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/dynamics-365/sales/tls-1-dot-2-required-for-connectivity>
* <https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/manage-encryption-key>

Reference the Enterprise Wide SDP, Protection Considerations section.
